newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Winterthur sees $500 mln China premiums.
newsitem.headline: Winterthur sees $500 mln China premiums.

text.p: Winterthur Insurance Co expects premium income from its Chinese non-life business to reach $500 million in 10 years, vice president Roger Schaerer said.
"Within the next 10 years we plan to have half a billion dollars in premium income. That is largely what we are planning," he told Reuters.
Winterthur said earlier that Chinese authorities had granted it a definitive licence for non-life insurance business in the Shanghai region and that it would start operations as early as next year.
He said the company would launch a unit called Winterthur Insurance Asia (Shanghai) and had already bought a property.
"We will build up a high-quality network there with local staff who will be trained by our people in Hong Kong. This is our main goal," he said.
Schaerer said the company saw China as a huge potential market.

"In Europe or the United States we have an average expenditure for insurance of around $3,000 per capita per year and in China it's about $3 to $5," he said. "And when you see the increasing industrial production and rising income of the Chinese people, there is really potential in the market."
Schaerer said Winterthur expected more foreign insurers to get licenses to conduct business in China.
"We think that Shanghai is a test market for the Chinese authorities. We think the Chinese authorities were afraid at first to have more foreign competitors," he said.
"But now they are opening steadily and I have some admiration for the really intelligent steps they make by opening their insurance market."
